name: What should be included in a pool removal quote?

mainEntity.name: Which line items should homeowners check so a pool demolition estimate is complete?
mainEntity.text: Which line items should homeowners check so a pool demolition estimate is complete?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pool removal quote should be specific enough that two contractors can be compared line by line. At minimum, it should state whether the project is partial or full removal, how much concrete or shell material will be hauled away, whether fill dirt and compaction are included, and what level of grading will be delivered at the end. The quote should also show permit handling, inspection coordination, debris disposal, and cleanup. If access is tight, the estimate should mention equipment size, hand work, or protection of existing surfaces. Homeowners should also look for exclusions such as turf, irrigation repair, hardscape replacement, retaining wall work, or final landscaping. A vague quote can look cheaper at first but become expensive once work starts. The best bids describe exactly what the yard will look like when the contractor leaves.
acceptedAnswer.description: A complete pool removal quote should list demolition, hauling, fill material, compaction, grading, permit handling, inspection coordination, and site cleanup. It should also identify whether the bid is for partial or full removal and what restoration work is included or excluded.
